risks.risk: EV transition and rapid technology change
risks.note: High initial EV cost, limited range, battery life/recyclability concerns and still-developing charging infrastructure are cited as barriers to EV adoption; management also flags 'Technology' (EVs, autonomous driving) as a distinct enterprise risk category that could reshape demand for the Company's bearing technologies.

risks.risk: Competition from low-cost imported bearings and counterfeit parts
risks.note: The sector faces intense competition from low-cost imported bearings and a growing incidence of counterfeit parts, which management flags as a threat to sustainable growth and consumer trust.
Fluctuating raw material prices are explicitly flagged as a sector challenge affecting cost structure and margins.

Management identifies currency risk as a financial risk under increased focus, with explicit triggers such as the Euro-Dollar rate or USD-INR rate exceeding a specified risk point, reflecting exposure via exports and foreign subsidiaries/step-down subsidiaries in Europe, USA and Thailand.

risks.risk: Evolving OEM requirements and platform consolidation
risks.note: Automotive OEMs are consolidating platforms to reduce complexity and demanding simpler, more versatile components usable across multiple platforms, requiring continuous product/engineering adaptation by the Company.

Rapidly evolving emissions and safety regulations, vehicle scrapping policy, and shifting standards (e.g., BS-VI-driven demand shifts) create both compliance risk and the need for continuous product realignment; inadequate compliance could lead to litigation and reputational loss.

Management flags risk of disruption to operations from a natural calamity or pandemic, alongside information-security (data leakage) and technology-disruption risks within its Operations risk category.

The need for skilled labour is flagged as a sector challenge alongside counterfeit parts, scrapping policy and import competition, relevant given the Company's large workforce (BRSR: 3,391 workers, of whom the large majority are 'other than permanent').

one-line thesis: NRB delivered strong FY26 growth (Rev +11%, PAT +77%) driven by volume gains and structural margin expansion to 19.5%, while successfully pivoting into high-margin aerospace via the Mahant Toolroom acquisition. The company is transitioning from capacity constraints to a growth phase with INR 120 Cr FY27 capex aimed at unlocking latent demand in both automotive and industrial segments.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 372 Cr (Q4, +13% YoY), INR 1,335 Cr (FY26, +11% YoY); EBITDA: INR 74 Cr (Q4, +17% YoY), INR 267 Cr (FY26, +19% YoY); Margin: 19.5% (Q4 & FY26, up from 18.3% FY25); PAT: INR 42 Cr (Q4), INR 146 Cr (FY26, +77% YoY); Order Book: Mahant Toolroom at INR 50 Cr (doubled from INR 25 Cr); Net Debt: Not explicitly quantified but capital allocation termed 'prudent'; One-offs: Q4 gross margin dip attributed to forex aberration on last-day booking and product mix, not structural.
guidance: Revenue Growth: International business expected to grow 10-15% in FY27 (vs 4% in FY26); Margins: Target range 18-21% sustained; Order Inflow: Aerospace defense rollout accelerating; Capex: INR 120 Cr for FY27 (part of INR 240 Cr over 18 months), commissioning starts June-July 2026.
order book & pipeline: Mahant Toolroom subsidiary holds INR 50 Cr order book (100% defense/HAL currently), doubling post-acquisition announcement; execution timeline dependent on defense rollout speeds rather than fixed 12-18 month window.
segment / subsidiary detail: Automotive focus on transmission, steering, and chassis (presence in Mercedes/BMW/ZF platforms); Industrial segment (14-15% of revenue) targeting construction, off-highway, and power generation; Aerospace entry via Mahant for mission-critical defense components (landing gear, fuel injection).
growth verticals / optionality: Industrial segment target to reach 20-25% of revenue mix within 3 years; Aerospace certification (AS 9100) expected within 6 months enabling commercial expansion; Import substitution opportunities via potential JVs for non-manufactured bearing types in India.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margins expanded to 19.5% driven by solar energy adoption, automation, yield improvements, and vendor cost renegotiation; Q4 gross margin volatility due to forex accounting timing, expected to normalize; Industrial segment margins expected to align with corporate 18-21% target.
capex / expansion: FY27 capex guidance INR 120 Cr (90% machinery, 10% infrastructure); part of broader INR 240 Cr plan over 18 months including INR 40 Cr for land; major enhancement projects commissioning June-July 2026 through Q1 2028.
capital allocation: Prudent approach focused on brownfield expansion to remove bottlenecks; strategic acquisition of Mahant Toolroom to accelerate aerospace entry (saving ~3 years of organic certification time); no dividend/buyback specifics mentioned, reinvestment prioritized.
risks & watch-items: Global geopolitical disruptions affecting logistics; Forex volatility impacting reported margins; Dependency on defense rollout speeds for Mahant revenue realization; Raw material (steel) price fluctuations.
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; emphasizes 'EV agnostic' model, engineering depth over commodity pricing, and resilience against global supply chain shocks; transparent about accounting anomalies but firm on long-term structural improvements.
non-obvious takeaways: Company explicitly rejects the traditional 'loss-leader OEM / high-margin aftermarket' model, maintaining consistent pricing discipline across channels; 'Mass customization' capability allows rapid adaptation to platform changes (ICE/Hybrid/EV) without margin erosion; Inventory strategy deliberately optimized (down INR 20 Cr despite sales growth) to enhance responsiveness rather than buffer stock.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for certified domestic suppliers for mission-critical defense aerospace components | Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd | beneficiary | High | NRB's Mahant subsidiary order book doubled to INR 50 Cr with explicit HAL endorsement; certification process underway to expand scope. |
| Transition to EV platforms risking bearing content per vehicle | NRB Bearings Limited | beneficiary | High | Management confirms 'EV agnostic' strategy with maintained margin profiles in EV-specific applications and increased content in e-steering systems. |
| Supply chain disruptions and gas shortages impacting production continuity | Competitors with rigid inventory models | loser | Med | NRB's optimized inventory and global positioning allowed uninterrupted supply while others faced constraints. |

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.
themes.driver: New commercial-aero RFP wins; engine-component capacity ramps; new MRO licences; Boeing/Airbus build-rate recovery.

themes.title: Bearings & motion-control localization
themes.need: Bearings and motion-control makers (MNC subs + domestic) ride an auto + industrial-aftermarket localization driver across automotive, railway, wind, off-highway and power-gen - distinct from machine-tool/process-equipment capex or pure OEM demand.
themes.driver: Auto + industrial/railway/wind/off-highway aftermarket localization and import-substitution.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian auto retail delivered a record year with total volumes of 2,96,71,064 units (13.30% YoY growth); five of six vehicle categories achieved highest-ever annual sales.
- Retail growth was moderate (2-5%) from April-August 2025 due to residual inventory caution and cautious consumer sentiment, then strengthened from September 2025 following GST 2.0, which reduced the effective tax burden on mass-segment two-wheelers, small cars, three-wheelers and select commercial vehicles; the October festive period delivered record retail volumes of over 40 lakh units.
- Automotive and industrial manufacturing sectors - key demand drivers for the bearing industry - are expected to benefit from rising manufacturing capacity utilisation, healthy credit growth, continued infrastructure development, GST rationalisation and resilient domestic demand.
- India's economic growth is projected stronger than peer economies, supported by robust domestic consumption, government infrastructure push, logistics development and industrial corridor development, which are expected to raise industrial competitiveness.
- Recent deceleration in EV demand could complicate the industry's near-term trajectory, though government initiatives such as the Automotive Mission Plan 2026, scrappage policy and production-linked incentive scheme are expected to support the two-wheeler and four-wheeler market.
- India is emerging as a global hub for auto component sourcing, with the industry exporting over 25% of its production annually; policy support includes 100% FDI allowed, no import-export restrictions, and a PLI scheme for automobile and auto components with an approved five-year outlay of Rs. 57,042 crores.
- India's cost-effective manufacturing base keeps costs 10-25% lower than operations in Europe and Latin America, with proximity to key automotive markets (ASEAN, Europe, Japan, Korea) an enabling factor.
- Global economic outlook anticipates a growth slowdown amid trade-policy uncertainty and geopolitical tensions, with China's rise as a disruptive force in autos prompting increased trade barriers and scrutiny from traditional leaders (Europe, US).
- Elevated energy/commodity prices, foreign exchange fluctuations, supply chain disruptions and geopolitical developments in West Asia are flagged as risks to economic growth, input costs, export demand and manufacturing-sector sentiment.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margins expanded to 19.5% driven by solar energy adoption, automation, yield improvements, and vendor cost renegotiation; Q4 gross margin volatility due to forex accounting timing, expected to normalize; Industrial segment margins expected to align with corporate 18-21% target.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prudent approach focused on brownfield expansion to remove bottlenecks; strategic acquisition of Mahant Toolroom to accelerate aerospace entry (saving ~3 years of organic certification time); no dividend/buyback specifics mentioned, reinvestment prioritized.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Board of Directors approved a series of capex investments during and after the year to strengthen the Company's presence across current-generation vehicle platforms and reinforce its position as a preferred supplier of high-precision bearing solutions to leading global and European automotive manufacturers: a capital expenditure programme approved on April 25, 2025; an additional investment for capacity expansion approved on February 9, 2026; and acquisition of a parcel of land for expansion purposes approved on May 7, 2026. These investments will be used for upgradation and expansion of manufacturing capacities across the Company's production facilities and its Research & Development (R&D) Centre. The proposed capacity expansion covers the Company's existing product portfolio - Taper Roller Bearings, Ball Bearings, Wide Inner Ring Bearings, Spherical Roller Bearings, Cylindrical Roller Bearings, Needle Roller Bearings, and Thrust Bearings - and, upon completion, is expected to enhance production capacity by approximately 15% to 25%, enabling the Company to cater to growing customer demand and support future business growth.
